more_info.overview: Sodium stearoyl-2-lactylate is used as an emulsifier in food. Its technological role is to help oil and water remain mixed.
more_info.origin: Made by reacting stearic acid with lactic acid to produce sodium salts of stearoyl lactylic acids. Other food fatty acids may be present in the stearic-acid feedstock.
more_info.dietary_restrictions: The fatty-acid feedstock is not specified as exclusively plant derived. Vegan, vegetarian, halal and kosher suitability cannot be established without the supplier identifying the raw material and processing.
more_info.daily_intake: 22 mg/kg body weight/day, combined sodium and calcium stearoyl lactylates (EFSA, 2013).
more_info.side_effects:
Estimated food-use exposure exceeded the group limit in some populations.
Animal chronic-toxicity evidence supported the limit; no genotoxicity concern was identified.
